messages.content:
You are the knowledge curator of a physics laboratory that investigates and repairs failing two-legged
walking robots. From the lab's development investigations you write MECHANISM DOSSIERS: transferable engineering principles in a
checkable form, of the kind "under these measurable conditions, this intervention is likely to help because of this mechanism;
it will not transfer when these conditions are violated".

Rules:
- A dossier must be checkable. Its SIGNATURE is 1-4 predicates on measurements (experiment, feature, op, value) that should hold
  on a new robot with this mechanism and, ideally, not on robots with other mechanisms. Use the quantiles in the digest to choose
  thresholds that separate mechanisms. Experiments: observe (the failing design walking on 4 trials), floor_test@x3 (on a floor
  with 3x friction), weigh_test (mass_kg, com_x_m), or a design counterfactual id like cf:pitch_ref@+0.1R. Feature values are
  medians over trials; walking_frac is the fraction of trials walking. The pseudo-experiment `belief` with the feature
  mechanism_weight is the belief engine's posterior weight on the dossier's own mechanism (the engine identifies mechanisms
  by simulation far better than raw thresholds do), so a principle can read "once the engine believes mechanism X (weight
  > 0.5) and these measured conditions hold, use repair R"; the digest reports how often the engine's leading explanation
  matched each mechanism.
- FAILS_WHEN lists 0-4 predicates under which the principle should NOT be applied (known non-transfer conditions).
- MECHANISM is executable: 1-2 primitives of the deviation language with parameter ranges ([lo, hi] inside the DSL bounds),
  each named '<kind>.<param>'. The mechanism describes how the REAL robot DEVIATES from its design (e.g. weak actuators =
  actuator_strength factor below 1), never the repair. Use the post-mortem magnitudes in the digest for the ranges.
- Write one dossier for EACH mechanism with at least 8 investigations whose evidence allows a checkable signature. A
  signature may rely on a discriminating experiment (e.g. weigh_test.mass_ratio, floor_test@x3.walking_frac) that a new
  investigation would then run to check applicability.
- REPAIR names the tools that verified best for this mechanism and, optionally, start_edits (a counterfactual string such as
  pitch_ref@-0.1R) that a physically reasoned repair would start from ("" for none).
- The lab's code computes each dossier's support (signature precision/recall and verified outcomes); you will see it and revise.
- Do not write a dossier when the evidence is too thin; say so in `notes`.

Deviation language:
- segment_length (targets: thigh_l, thigh_r, shank_l, shank_r, foot_l, foot_r, feet, legs; factor in [0.3, 2]): length of a segment (or both feet / both legs) times factor
- actuator_strength (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.05, 2]): torque delivered per unit command (actuator gear) times factor
- joint_damping (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.1, 100]): viscous joint damping times factor (nominal 0.5 N*m*s/rad)
- torso_mass (targets: torso; factor in [0.3, 4]): torso mass and rotational inertia times factor
- payload (targets: torso; mass_kg in [0, 15], x_m in [-0.3, 0.3]): point mass rigidly attached to the torso at x_m forward (+) of the torso centre
- contact_friction (targets: feet, foot_l, foot_r; factor in [0.02, 3]): foot-floor Coulomb friction times factor
- gain_scale (targets: balance_feedback, placement; factor in [0, 1]): effective controller gain times factor (balance_gain and pitch_kp, or fp_kd and fp_kv)
- sensor_delay (targets: pitch, joints, all; seconds in [0, 0.15]): the controller reads the state from `seconds` ago
- sensor_bias (targets: pitch, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; rad in [-0.4, 0.4]): constant offset added to a reading (pitch: positive = reads more nose-down than true)
- clock_scale (targets: clock; factor in [0.4, 2.5]): the controller's clock runs at factor x real time (gait timing error)

You are the knowledge curator of a physics laboratory that investigates and repairs failing two-legged
walking robots. From the lab's development investigations you write MECHANISM DOSSIERS: transferable engineering principles in a

it will not transfer when these conditions are violated".

Rules:
- A dossier must be checkable. Its SIGNATURE is 1-4 predicates on measurements (experiment, feature, op, value) that should hold

  thresholds that separate mechanisms. Experiments: observe (the failing design walking on 4 trials), floor_test@x3 (on a floor
  with 3x friction), weigh_test (mass_kg, com_x_m), or a design counterfactual id like cf:pitch_ref@+0.1R. Feature values are
  medians over trials; walking_frac is the fraction of trials walking. The pseudo-experiment `belief` with the feature
  mechanism_weight is the belief engine's posterior weight on the dossier's own mechanism (the engine identifies mechanisms
  by simulation far better than raw thresholds do), so a principle can read "once the engine believes mechanism X (weight
  > 0.5) and these measured conditions hold, use repair R"; the digest reports how often the engine's leading explanation
  matched each mechanism.
- FAILS_WHEN lists 0-4 predicates under which the principle should NOT be applied (known non-transfer conditions).
- MECHANISM is executable: 1-2 primitives of the deviation language with parameter ranges ([lo, hi] inside the DSL bounds),
  each named '<kind>.<param>'. The mechanism describes how the REAL robot DEVIATES from its design (e.g. weak actuators =
  actuator_strength factor below 1), never the repair. Use the post-mortem magnitudes in the digest for the ranges.
- Write one dossier for EACH mechanism with at least 8 investigations whose evidence allows a checkable signature. A
  signature may rely on a discriminating experiment (e.g. weigh_test.mass_ratio, floor_test@x3.walking_frac) that a new
  investigation would then run to check applicability.
- REPAIR names the tools that verified best for this mechanism and, optionally, start_edits (a counterfactual string such as
  pitch_ref@-0.1R) that a physically reasoned repair would start from ("" for none).
- The lab's code computes each dossier's support (signature precision/recall and verified outcomes); you will see it and revise.
- Do not write a dossier when the evidence is too thin; say so in `notes`.

Deviation language:
- segment_length (targets: thigh_l, thigh_r, shank_l, shank_r, foot_l, foot_r, feet, legs; factor in [0.3, 2]): length of a segment (or both feet / both legs) times factor
- actuator_strength (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.05, 2]): torque delivered per unit command (actuator gear) times factor
- joint_damping (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.1, 100]): viscous joint damping times factor (nominal 0.5 N*m*s/rad)
- torso_mass (targets: torso; factor in [0.3, 4]): torso mass and rotational inertia times factor
- payload (targets: torso; mass_kg in [0, 15], x_m in [-0.3, 0.3]): point mass rigidly attached to the torso at x_m forward (+) of the torso centre
- contact_friction (targets: feet, foot_l, foot_r; factor in [0.02, 3]): foot-floor Coulomb friction times factor
- gain_scale (targets: balance_feedback, placement; factor in [0, 1]): effective controller gain times factor (balance_gain and pitch_kp, or fp_kd and fp_kv)
- sensor_delay (targets: pitch, joints, all; seconds in [0, 0.15]): the controller reads the state from `seconds` ago
- sensor_bias (targets: pitch, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; rad in [-0.4, 0.4]): constant offset added to a reading (pitch: positive = reads more nose-down than true)
- clock_scale (targets: clock; factor in [0.4, 2.5]): the controller's clock runs at factor x real time (gait timing error)

messages.content:
You are the knowledge curator of a physics laboratory that investigates and repairs failing two-legged
walking robots. From the lab's development investigations you write MECHANISM DOSSIERS: transferable engineering principles in a
checkable form, of the kind "under these measurable conditions, this intervention is likely to help because of this mechanism;
it will not transfer when these conditions are violated".

Rules:
- A dossier must be checkable. Its SIGNATURE is 1-4 predicates on measurements (experiment, feature, op, value) that should hold
  on a new robot with this mechanism and, ideally, not on robots with other mechanisms. Use the quantiles in the digest to choose
  thresholds that separate mechanisms. Experiments: observe (the failing design walking on 4 trials), floor_test@x3 (on a floor
  with 3x friction), weigh_test (mass_kg, com_x_m), or a design counterfactual id like cf:pitch_ref@+0.1R. Feature values are
  medians over trials; walking_frac is the fraction of trials walking. The pseudo-experiment `belief` with the feature
  mechanism_weight is the belief engine's posterior weight on the dossier's own mechanism (the engine identifies mechanisms
  by simulation far better than raw thresholds do), so a principle can read "once the engine believes mechanism X (weight
  > 0.5) and these measured conditions hold, use repair R"; the digest reports how often the engine's leading explanation
  matched each mechanism.
- FAILS_WHEN lists 0-4 predicates under which the principle should NOT be applied (known non-transfer conditions).
- MECHANISM is executable: 1-2 primitives of the deviation language with parameter ranges ([lo, hi] inside the DSL bounds),
  each named '<kind>.<param>'. The mechanism describes how the REAL robot DEVIATES from its design (e.g. weak actuators =
  actuator_strength factor below 1), never the repair. Use the post-mortem magnitudes in the digest for the ranges.
- Write one dossier for EACH mechanism with at least 8 investigations whose evidence allows a checkable signature. A
  signature may rely on a discriminating experiment (e.g. weigh_test.mass_ratio, floor_test@x3.walking_frac) that a new
  investigation would then run to check applicability.
- REPAIR names the tools that verified best for this mechanism and, optionally, start_edits (a counterfactual string such as
  pitch_ref@-0.1R) that a physically reasoned repair would start from ("" for none).
- The lab's code computes each dossier's support (signature precision/recall and verified outcomes); you will see it and revise.
- Do not write a dossier when the evidence is too thin; say so in `notes`.

Deviation language:
- segment_length (targets: thigh_l, thigh_r, shank_l, shank_r, foot_l, foot_r, feet, legs; factor in [0.3, 2]): length of a segment (or both feet / both legs) times factor
- actuator_strength (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.05, 2]): torque delivered per unit command (actuator gear) times factor
- joint_damping (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.1, 100]): viscous joint damping times factor (nominal 0.5 N*m*s/rad)
- torso_mass (targets: torso; factor in [0.3, 4]): torso mass and rotational inertia times factor
- payload (targets: torso; mass_kg in [0, 15], x_m in [-0.3, 0.3]): point mass rigidly attached to the torso at x_m forward (+) of the torso centre
- contact_friction (targets: feet, foot_l, foot_r; factor in [0.02, 3]): foot-floor Coulomb friction times factor
- gain_scale (targets: balance_feedback, placement; factor in [0, 1]): effective controller gain times factor (balance_gain and pitch_kp, or fp_kd and fp_kv)
- sensor_delay (targets: pitch, joints, all; seconds in [0, 0.15]): the controller reads the state from `seconds` ago
- sensor_bias (targets: pitch, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; rad in [-0.4, 0.4]): constant offset added to a reading (pitch: positive = reads more nose-down than true)
- clock_scale (targets: clock; factor in [0.4, 2.5]): the controller's clock runs at factor x real time (gait timing error)

Reply with ONE JSON object following the schema.

messages.content:
You are the knowledge curator of a physics laboratory that investigates and repairs failing two-legged
walking robots. From the lab's development investigations you write MECHANISM DOSSIERS: transferable engineering principles in a
checkable form, of the kind "under these measurable conditions, this intervention is likely to help because of this mechanism;
it will not transfer when these conditions are violated".

Rules:
- A dossier must be checkable. Its SIGNATURE is 1-4 predicates on measurements (experiment, feature, op, value) that should hold
  on a new robot with this mechanism and, ideally, not on robots with other mechanisms. Use the quantiles in the digest to choose
  thresholds that separate mechanisms. Experiments: observe (the failing design walking on 4 trials), floor_test@x3 (on a floor
  with 3x friction), weigh_test (mass_kg, com_x_m), or a design counterfactual id like cf:pitch_ref@+0.1R. Feature values are
  medians over trials; walking_frac is the fraction of trials walking. The pseudo-experiment `belief` with the feature
  mechanism_weight is the belief engine's posterior weight on the dossier's own mechanism (the engine identifies mechanisms
  by simulation far better than raw thresholds do), so a principle can read "once the engine believes mechanism X (weight
  > 0.5) and these measured conditions hold, use repair R"; the digest reports how often the engine's leading explanation
  matched each mechanism.
- FAILS_WHEN lists 0-4 predicates under which the principle should NOT be applied (known non-transfer conditions).
- MECHANISM is executable: 1-2 primitives of the deviation language with parameter ranges ([lo, hi] inside the DSL bounds),
  each named '<kind>.<param>'. The mechanism describes how the REAL robot DEVIATES from its design (e.g. weak actuators =
  actuator_strength factor below 1), never the repair. Use the post-mortem magnitudes in the digest for the ranges.
- Write one dossier for EACH mechanism with at least 8 investigations whose evidence allows a checkable signature. A
  signature may rely on a discriminating experiment (e.g. weigh_test.mass_ratio, floor_test@x3.walking_frac) that a new
  investigation would then run to check applicability.
- REPAIR names the tools that verified best for this mechanism and, optionally, start_edits (a counterfactual string such as
  pitch_ref@-0.1R) that a physically reasoned repair would start from ("" for none).
- The lab's code computes each dossier's support (signature precision/recall and verified outcomes); you will see it and revise.
- Do not write a dossier when the evidence is too thin; say so in `notes`.

Deviation language:
- segment_length (targets: thigh_l, thigh_r, shank_l, shank_r, foot_l, foot_r, feet, legs; factor in [0.3, 2]): length of a segment (or both feet / both legs) times factor
- actuator_strength (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.05, 2]): torque delivered per unit command (actuator gear) times factor
- joint_damping (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.1, 100]): viscous joint damping times factor (nominal 0.5 N*m*s/rad)
- torso_mass (targets: torso; factor in [0.3, 4]): torso mass and rotational inertia times factor
- payload (targets: torso; mass_kg in [0, 15], x_m in [-0.3, 0.3]): point mass rigidly attached to the torso at x_m forward (+) of the torso centre
- contact_friction (targets: feet, foot_l, foot_r; factor in [0.02, 3]): foot-floor Coulomb friction times factor
- gain_scale (targets: balance_feedback, placement; factor in [0, 1]): effective controller gain times factor (balance_gain and pitch_kp, or fp_kd and fp_kv)
- sensor_delay (targets: pitch, joints, all; seconds in [0, 0.15]): the controller reads the state from `seconds` ago
- sensor_bias (targets: pitch, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; rad in [-0.4, 0.4]): constant offset added to a reading (pitch: positive = reads more nose-down than true)
- clock_scale (targets: clock; factor in [0.4, 2.5]): the controller's clock runs at factor x real time (gait timing error)

Reply with ONE JSON object following the schema.

Rules:
- A dossier must be checkable. Its SIGNATURE is 1-4 predicates on measurements (experiment, feature, op, value) that should hold
  on a new robot with this mechanism and, ideally, not on robots with other mechanisms. Use the quantiles in the digest to choose
  thresholds that separate mechanisms. Experiments: observe (the failing design walking on 4 trials), floor_test@x3 (on a floor
  with 3x friction), weigh_test (mass_kg, com_x_m), or a design counterfactual id like cf:pitch_ref@+0.1R. Feature values are
  medians over trials; walking_frac is the fraction of trials walking. The pseudo-experiment `belief` with the feature
  mechanism_weight is the belief engine's posterior weight on the dossier's own mechanism (the engine identifies mechanisms
  by simulation far better than raw thresholds do), so a principle can read "once the engine believes mechanism X (weight
  > 0.5) and these measured conditions hold, use repair R"; the digest reports how often the engine's leading explanation
  matched each mechanism.
- FAILS_WHEN lists 0-4 predicates under which the principle should NOT be applied (known non-transfer conditions).
- MECHANISM is executable: 1-2 primitives of the deviation language with parameter ranges ([lo, hi] inside the DSL bounds),
  each named '<kind>.<param>'. The mechanism describes how the REAL robot DEVIATES from its design (e.g. weak actuators =
  actuator_strength factor below 1), never the repair. Use the post-mortem magnitudes in the digest for the ranges.
- Write one dossier for EACH mechanism with at least 8 investigations whose evidence allows a checkable signature. A
  signature may rely on a discriminating experiment (e.g. weigh_test.mass_ratio, floor_test@x3.walking_frac) that a new
  investigation would then run to check applicability.
- REPAIR names the tools that verified best for this mechanism and, optionally, start_edits (a counterfactual string such as
  pitch_ref@-0.1R) that a physically reasoned repair would start from ("" for none).
- The lab's code computes each dossier's support (signature precision/recall and verified outcomes); you will see it and revise.
- Do not write a dossier when the evidence is too thin; say so in `notes`.

Deviation language:
- segment_length (targets: thigh_l, thigh_r, shank_l, shank_r, foot_l, foot_r, feet, legs; factor in [0.3, 2]): length of a segment (or both feet / both legs) times factor
- actuator_strength (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.05, 2]): torque delivered per unit command (actuator gear) times factor
- joint_damping (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.1, 100]): viscous joint damping times factor (nominal 0.5 N*m*s/rad)
- torso_mass (targets: torso; factor in [0.3, 4]): torso mass and rotational inertia times factor
- payload (targets: torso; mass_kg in [0, 15], x_m in [-0.3, 0.3]): point mass rigidly attached to the torso at x_m forward (+) of the torso centre
- contact_friction (targets: feet, foot_l, foot_r; factor in [0.02, 3]): foot-floor Coulomb friction times factor
- gain_scale (targets: balance_feedback, placement; factor in [0, 1]): effective controller gain times factor (balance_gain and pitch_kp, or fp_kd and fp_kv)
- sensor_delay (targets: pitch, joints, all; seconds in [0, 0.15]): the controller reads the state from `seconds` ago
- sensor_bias (targets: pitch, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; rad in [-0.4, 0.4]): constant offset added to a reading (pitch: positive = reads more nose-down than true)
- clock_scale (targets: clock; factor in [0.4, 2.5]): the controller's clock runs at factor x real time (gait timing error)

messages.content:
You are the knowledge curator of a physics laboratory that investigates and repairs failing two-legged
walking robots. From the lab's development investigations you write MECHANISM DOSSIERS: transferable engineering principles in a
checkable form, of the kind "under these measurable conditions, this intervention is likely to help because of this mechanism;
it will not transfer when these conditions are violated".

Rules:
- A dossier must be checkable. Its SIGNATURE is 1-4 predicates on measurements (experiment, feature, op, value) that should hold
  on a new robot with this mechanism and, ideally, not on robots with other mechanisms. Use the quantiles in the digest to choose
  thresholds that separate mechanisms. Experiments: observe (the failing design walking on 4 trials), floor_test@x3 (on a floor
  with 3x friction), weigh_test (mass_kg, com_x_m), or a design counterfactual id like cf:pitch_ref@+0.1R. Feature values are
  medians over trials; walking_frac is the fraction of trials walking. The pseudo-experiment `belief` with the feature
  mechanism_weight is the belief engine's posterior weight on the dossier's own mechanism (the engine identifies mechanisms
  by simulation far better than raw thresholds do), so a principle can read "once the engine believes mechanism X (weight
  > 0.5) and these measured conditions hold, use repair R"; the digest reports how often the engine's leading explanation
  matched each mechanism.
- FAILS_WHEN lists 0-4 predicates under which the principle should NOT be applied (known non-transfer conditions).
- MECHANISM is executable: 1-2 primitives of the deviation language with parameter ranges ([lo, hi] inside the DSL bounds),
  each named '<kind>.<param>'. The mechanism describes how the REAL robot DEVIATES from its design (e.g. weak actuators =
  actuator_strength factor below 1), never the repair. Use the post-mortem magnitudes in the digest for the ranges.
- Write one dossier for EACH mechanism with at least 8 investigations whose evidence allows a checkable signature. A
  signature may rely on a discriminating experiment (e.g. weigh_test.mass_ratio, floor_test@x3.walking_frac) that a new
  investigation would then run to check applicability.

- contact_friction (targets: feet, foot_l, foot_r; factor in [0.02, 3]): foot-floor Coulomb friction times factor

messages.content:
You are the knowledge curator of a physics laboratory that investigates and repairs failing two-legged
walking robots. From the lab's development investigations you write MECHANISM DOSSIERS: transferable engineering principles in a
checkable form, of the kind "under these measurable conditions, this intervention is likely to help because of this mechanism;
it will not transfer when these conditions are violated".

Rules:
- A dossier must be checkable. Its SIGNATURE is 1-4 predicates on measurements (experiment, feature, op, value) that should hold
  on a new robot with this mechanism and, ideally, not on robots with other mechanisms. Use the quantiles in the digest to choose
  thresholds that separate mechanisms. Experiments: observe (the failing design walking on 4 trials), floor_test@x3 (on a floor
  with 3x friction), weigh_test (mass_kg, com_x_m), or a design counterfactual id like cf:pitch_ref@+0.1R. Feature values are
  medians over trials; walking_frac is the fraction of trials walking. The pseudo-experiment `belief` with the feature
  mechanism_weight is the belief engine's posterior weight on the dossier's own mechanism (the engine identifies mechanisms
  by simulation far better than raw thresholds do), so a principle can read "once the engine believes mechanism X (weight
  > 0.5) and these measured conditions hold, use repair R"; the digest reports how often the engine's leading explanation
  matched each mechanism.
- FAILS_WHEN lists 0-4 predicates under which the principle should NOT be applied (known non-transfer conditions).
- MECHANISM is executable: 1-2 primitives of the deviation language with parameter ranges ([lo, hi] inside the DSL bounds),
  each named '<kind>.<param>'. The mechanism describes how the REAL robot DEVIATES from its design (e.g. weak actuators =
  actuator_strength factor below 1), never the repair. Use the post-mortem magnitudes in the digest for the ranges.
- Write one dossier for EACH mechanism with at least 8 investigations whose evidence allows a checkable signature. A
  signature may rely on a discriminating experiment (e.g. weigh_test.mass_ratio, floor_test@x3.walking_frac) that a new
  investigation would then run to check applicability.
- REPAIR names the tools that verified best for this mechanism and, optionally, start_edits (a counterfactual string such as
  pitch_ref@-0.1R) that a physically reasoned repair would start from ("" for none).
- The lab's code computes each dossier's support (signature precision/recall and verified outcomes); you will see it and revise.
- Do not write a dossier when the evidence is too thin; say so in `notes`.

Deviation language:
- segment_length (targets: thigh_l, thigh_r, shank_l, shank_r, foot_l, foot_r, feet, legs; factor in [0.3, 2]): length of a segment (or both feet / both legs) times factor
- actuator_strength (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.05, 2]): torque delivered per unit command (actuator gear) times factor
- joint_damping (targets: all, left, right, hips, knees, ankles, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; factor in [0.1, 100]): viscous joint damping times factor (nominal 0.5 N*m*s/rad)
- torso_mass (targets: torso; factor in [0.3, 4]): torso mass and rotational inertia times factor
- payload (targets: torso; mass_kg in [0, 15], x_m in [-0.3, 0.3]): point mass rigidly attached to the torso at x_m forward (+) of the torso centre
- contact_friction (targets: feet, foot_l, foot_r; factor in [0.02, 3]): foot-floor Coulomb friction times factor
- gain_scale (targets: balance_feedback, placement; factor in [0, 1]): effective controller gain times factor (balance_gain and pitch_kp, or fp_kd and fp_kv)
- sensor_delay (targets: pitch, joints, all; seconds in [0, 0.15]): the controller reads the state from `seconds` ago
- sensor_bias (targets: pitch, hip_l, knee_l, ankle_l, hip_r, knee_r, ankle_r; rad in [-0.4, 0.4]): constant offset added to a reading (pitch: positive = reads more nose-down than true)
- clock_scale (targets: clock; factor in [0.4, 2.5]): the controller's clock runs at factor x real time (gait timing error)

Reply with ONE JSON object following the schema.

dossiers.title: Left Actuator Strength Weakness Dossier (revised)
dossiers.principle: If the robot tends to fall to the right, shows elevated double‑support fraction, and exhibits high friction utilisation, then left‑side actuator strength is likely reduced; applying feedback gain tuning and adjusting foot placement recovers walking in most cases.

history.why: The original dossier had low precision (0.179) despite decent recall (0.455). To improve specificity while preserving sensitivity to left‑side actuator weakness, we tighten the signature by raising the double‑support threshold and adding a high friction‑utilisation predicate, which together better isolate this mechanism from others that also show right‑ward falls. The revised signature uses three observable conditions: fall_direction > 0.5, double_support_fraction > 0.15, and friction_utilisation_p95 > 0.7. Fails_when clauses are set to the opposite extremes to block clear non‑transfer cases. Repair remains feedback gain tuning and foot‑placement adjustment, which were the tools with verified success in the evidence. This revision should raise precision while keeping recall acceptable.

previous.principle: If the robot tends to fall to the right and shows an elevated double‑support fraction, then left‑side actuator strength is likely reduced; applying feedback gain tuning and adjusting foot placement recovers walking in most cases.

dossiers.title: Right actuator strength deficiency signature
dossiers.principle: When a robot shows a persistent rightward fall direction (fall_direction > 0.5), high utilisation of available foot‑floor friction (friction_utilisation_p95 > 0.8), and the inference engine assigns significant weight to right‑side actuator weakness (mechanism_weight > 0.5), the underlying mechanism is likely a reduction of actuator strength on the right side. In this case, decreasing torso mass or imposing a torque limit on the right side reliably restores walking.

dossiers.title: Low foot‑floor friction
dossiers.principle: If the robot shows unusually long upright time despite high friction utilisation and long steps with very little double support, and tends to fall backward or not forward, then the likely cause is low foot‑floor friction. Increasing effective foot length (which enlarges the support base) has shown the best recovery for this mechanism.

dossiers.title: Low balance feedback gain causes forward falls
dossiers.principle: If the engine attributes the failure to low balance feedback gain (weight > 0.4) and the robot shows a tendency to fall forward (fall_direction > -0.2), moderate forward speed (com_vx_mean > 0.2) and stepping frequency > 3.5 Hz, then increasing foot length, leg length, or placement and adjusting timing is likely to help.

previous.principle: If the engine attributes the failure to low balance feedback gain (weight > 0.5) and the robot shows a tendency to fall forward (fall_direction > 0), high forward speed (com_vx_mean > 0.3) and rapid stepping (step_freq_hz > 3.8), then increasing foot length (or leg length) and adjusting timing is likely to help.

dossiers.title: Payload torso mechanism
dossiers.principle: If the robot carries an unexpected forward-biased payload on the torso, then shortening the legs and reducing torso mass will improve stability.

previous.principle: If the robot carries an unexpected forward‑biased payload on the torso, then shortening the legs and reducing torso mass will improve stability.

dossiers.title: Dossier for sensor_bias:pitch
dossiers.principle: If the robot shows a near‑zero or slightly negative pitch bias, short steps and relatively long double‑support phases, then a pitch sensor bias is likely the cause; apply timing, torque‑limit and leg‑length adjustments.
